title: Library of the Citadel story record
description: One literary work on a Library of the Citadel story shelf. A story is not a knowledge record: it makes no factual claim, cites nothing, and is published as its author's own text. Its body has exactly one canonical language and is never machine-translated, so — unlike a knowledge item, whose canonical text is English with additive overlays — a story carries its reader-facing metadata for every interface locale inside the record itself, under "locales". That keeps the body single-sourced and makes the record portable: a consumer needs no overlay file and no Library presentation code to render it in either language.

record_class.description: The only class a story shelf holds. It says what the text is: an original work of fiction written for this Library, not a sourced record, not a fixture, and not a claim about the world.

publication_ready.description: True only for a work its author has released. Unlike a knowledge record, a story has no factual or safety review to pass; src/stories.mjs instead requires a released story to name its author, state its genre and publication note in every locale, and claim no source or authority.

canonical.description: The title as the author wrote it, in the language of the body. Every locale shows this alongside its own rendering, so no reader is left thinking a translated title is the work's name.

body_language.description: BCP 47 tag for the body. The body is published in this language in every locale and is never machine-translated.

body.description: The literary text as ordered blocks. Plain data: no markup, no markdown, nothing a renderer has to parse. A paragraph carries "text"; a verse carries "stanzas", each a list of lines. "emphasis" lists exact substrings to render as strong; src/stories.mjs rejects one that does not occur in the block.

body_block_count.description: Declared length of "body". A published literary text must not lose a paragraph to a careless edit, so the count is written down and checked against the array on every build.

acknowledgements.description: People credited beside the author. The role is prose and therefore lives in each locale's "acknowledgement" string; only the name and an optional canonical URL are held here.

sources.description: Always empty for an original work. A story that ever needs a citation is not this class of record.

locales.description: Reader-facing metadata per interface locale. Every locale in src/i18n.mjs must be present and complete; src/stories.mjs checks that parity, so a story can never render a half-written page or fall back to a language the reader did not ask for.

en.description: The validated subset in src/schema-validate.mjs has no $ref, so each locale states the same shape in full rather than pointing at a definition the validator would silently ignore.
